methods.name: NIH iSearch 'Predicted breakthroughs in biomedicine' / NIH OPA co-citation trajectory method
methods.type: public platform documentation (iSearch) + public preprint + restricted-licence code
methods.licence_or_terms: Preprint on bioRxiv (no reuse licence asserted on the page read). Code README, verbatim: 'Use of this software requires a license. No rights are granted beyond the view access permitted by the GitHub Terms and Conditions.' Data: figshare snapshot linked from the paper's Data/Code page; licence not verified (short-link resolution returned HTTP 202).
methods.data_public: partial (figshare citation snapshot linked; supplementary Data S1-S7 not retrieved)
methods.access_barrier: iSearch article itself unreachable: Cloudflare Error 1034 'Edge IP Restricted', HTTP 403, host resolving to an IP the owner does not control (2026-11-08). Code licence requires contacting authors. Compute: CCN needs >=384GB RAM, latest-year R-MCL needs ~350GB JVM.
methods.core_method: Cosine-similarity co-citation network of PubMed (17.2M papers through 2017, edge threshold 0.35) -> R-MCL clustering (inflation 1.2, maxIterations 500) -> ~23,867 topic clusters -> yearly networks (1981-2017, built only from data up to each terminal year) -> trajectory linking by simple majority paper overlap -> four features at each terminal cluster (%New over a two-year window, ancestral %New, entropy cohesion, contemporaneous-only influence whRCR) -> logistic regression on 21 award-curated gold-standard trajectories -> applied to 186,449 clusters in 1994-97 (setA) and 2014-17 (setB) with filters >=40 papers and >=5% NIH-award-linked.
data_deps: PubMed co-citation graph (17.2M cited papers, 750M citations via NIH open citation collection)
MongoDB citation snapshot restored from figshare
gold-standard label tables (21 breakthroughs 1984-2014; 13 Nobel + 3 Lasker)
NIH award linkage per paper (for the >=5% filter)
350-400 GB RAM class server (README positions this as an AWS EC2 job)
methods.overlap_with_medradar: Low on substrate (no citation graph, no papers, no award labels). Moderate on principles: strict point-in-time network construction, two-year recency-burst share, entropy as a concentration measure.
methods_to_migrate: point-in-time snapshot discipline: features computable only from data available at t (maps to MedRadar available_at/as_of)
pct_new-style recency burst: share of a track's activity in year x and x-1
entropy-based diversification (1 - H/log k) as a companion to HHI
majority-overlap trajectory chaining as a way to track a track/product-code lineage across years
limitations: ground truth = Nobel/Lasker recognition; no complete true-positive set, so precision/recall are not computable (authors state this)
21 curated successes as the positive class = case-control design with hand-curated cases
recognition lag inflates apparent lead time
~20% cluster churn (80% stability over 30 years) means historical signals are not exactly reproducible
compute-locked at 384GB RAM; code licence blocks reuse
preprint, not peer-reviewed at audit time
iSearch product documentation offline, so product behaviour cannot be verified at all
leakage_risks: co-citation weights must be recomputed per snapshot year; using final-network weights leaks future citations into past signals
award dates used as labels post-date the discovery, so a naive label timestamp leaks forward
in-sample gold standards inside setA inflate its apparent accuracy
methods.reproduction_status: NOT_REPRODUCED (no licence, no 384GB compute, no label tables). Feature logic (two-year %New, ancestral %New, entropy cohesion, contemporaneous-only influence, majority-overlap linking) independently re-implemented and self-tested on synthetic data: %New two-year window verified (0.500 vs 0.25 for a one-year window), leakage guard verified (1995 snapshot ignores a 2000 citation: 4.0 not 104.0), planted 3-year trajectory recovered by chaining.
methods.decision_reason: The published method is precise and has public source, but the code licence ('requires a license'), the 350-400GB compute requirement, and the missing supplementary label tables make independent reproduction impossible here; the product documentation that the task names is offline at the vendor's edge; and MedRadar has neither a citation graph nor award-based labels. Two design principles plus the recency-burst and entropy features are worth migrating and are implemented in trajectory_features.py.

methods.name: The Lens — paper/patent linkage (PatCite), citation structure, time-lag, access terms
methods.licence_or_terms: Terms of Use v2026.06.01: use conditions 'intended to resonate with the principles of Creative Commons attribution license CC BY-NC-SA including retention of Lens IDs'; attribution ('Enabled by The Lens' + logo + URL) mandatory; automated crawling/scraping explicitly prohibited; commercial use requires a commercial licence. API Terms v2026.06.01: API service 'only available through an institutional subscription'; trial access non-commercial for evaluation only, manually approved, token-based.
methods.data_public: partial, browser-only: anonymous users may export up to 1,000 records; no bulk, no scraping, no free programmatic tier
methods.access_barrier: No free public API. Institutional subscription + manual approval + token required for api.lens.org. Bulk data is a paid product. Trial plans are non-commercial evaluation only. Automated extraction is contractually prohibited.
methods.core_method: Non-patent-literature (NPL) reference strings in patent documents resolved against PubMed (PMID) and Crossref (DOI) at a cosine/string matching score threshold of 0.9 -> resolved citation edges patent-family <-> scholarly article -> patent to technology field via WIPO IPC->35-field concordance, article to discipline via ISSN/Crossref->9 disciplines -> In4M intensity metric = sum of family-size-weighted third-party patent citations / total resolved articles.
data_deps: patent corpus with NPL citations (EPO citation database, 30+ authorities; Lens holds 153.2M patents / 417M citations)
scholarly corpus with identifiers (266M works / 2.1B citations)
PubMed and Crossref metadata as resolution targets
WIPO IPC -> 35 technology-field concordance; ISSN -> discipline mapping
methods.overlap_with_medradar: Near zero on data (MedRadar holds no patents and no scholarly works). Conceptual overlap: group-size normalisation of an attention signal, and explicit match thresholds with a reported resolution rate for free-text joins (the analogue is applicant-name -> company_key).
methods_to_migrate: explicit fuzzy-match threshold with a reported resolution rate when joining free-text entity names
family/group-size weighting to normalise an attention or citation signal across groups
attribution and licence obligations if any Lens-derived number is ever used
limitations: only ~45% of NPL strings resolve (14.1M/31.6M), and resolution quality varies by era and jurisdiction
citation-reporting bias across jurisdictions, document locations and prosecution history (authors' own caveat)
field skew concentrated in pharma/biotech, i.e. not transferable to devices
time-lag distribution is not published by The Lens in any source I could access
bespoke, non-open licence: 'CC BY-NC-SA-resonant' is not CC BY-NC-SA
paper is CC BY-NC-ND (no derivatives) while platform data is separately licensed
leakage_risks: patent publication/grant date is after the citation event; measuring lag from publication rather than priority/filing leaks future information
resolution missingness is correlated with era and jurisdiction, so lag and intensity statistics inherit a time-dependent bias
examiner-added citations post-date invention and can appear years after filing
methods.reproduction_status: NOT_REPRODUCED and deliberately not attempted: the terms prohibit automated extraction and bulk download, and the API requires an institutional token. NO Lens data was queried during this audit. The linkage pipeline shape (0.9 threshold against PubMed/Crossref, family-size weighting, In4M ratio) was extracted from the CC BY method paper and recorded, but it cannot be exercised lawfully on Lens data here.
methods.decision_reason: Bulk and automated access are contractually prohibited without an institutional subscription, trial access is explicitly non-commercial, and there is no free public API tier; MedRadar additionally has neither a patent corpus nor a scholarly citation corpus to link. The method is well described but unusable under the audited terms. Transferable value is limited to two design patterns and an attribution obligation.

methods.name: PTNS — patent citation trajectory prediction based on temporal network snapshots
methods.type: public paper (peer-reviewed, open access CC BY-NC-ND)
methods.licence_or_terms: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 per Europe PMC metadata ('cc by-nc-nd'); non-commercial, no derivatives
methods.access_barrier: Publisher PDF requires an identity-provider redirect; full text read from PMC11473824. No code-availability statement and no repository link anywhere in the article. Data statement: 'The data shall be made available on request from the first author or the corresponding author.' Source corpus is Incopat, a commercial patent database. Replication needs a CUDA GPU (RTX 4060 class) and ~46 min per run x3.
methods.core_method: Yearly network snapshots (2004-2023) over four relations (IPC classification, citation, applicant, country); 2-layer R-GCN encodes relational attributes per snapshot with inter-snapshot alignment; BiLSTM aggregates temporal evolution with high/low weights for primary IPC and first applicant; PCA then four MLPs emit the parameters of a Richards (generalised logistic) growth curve; evaluated with MALE and RMSLE on new (<2 citations), grown (>4) and random patents over horizons T+1..T+10; baselines TGNN, HINTS, HDGNN, DeepCCP; 3 runs averaged, 35 epochs.
data_deps: Incopat patent corpus: 133,857 invention + utility-model patents, publication years 2004-2023, polyurethane field
per-patent IPC codes, applicants (first vs others), publication country, citation list, publication/application dates
yearly graph snapshots with node alignment across years
methods.overlap_with_medradar: Low on target and substrate: MedRadar has no patent citations and no citation-like attention graph. Moderate on protocol: multi-horizon backtesting with log-error metrics, and curve fitting of a cumulative traction series.
methods_to_migrate: multi-horizon rolling-origin evaluation with MALE/RMSLE reported per horizon (implemented in rolling_origin_backtest)
Richards / generalised logistic fitting for cumulative traction series (track-level authorisations, recalls, trials)
explicit subtask stratification so easy and hard trajectories are not pooled into one average
limitations: no code, no data -> results unverifiable and unreproducible
equations 1,2,4,5,6,7 are raster images in the published HTML; the prose alone is insufficient for exact re-implementation
internal inconsistency: Introduction says the case study is 'aviation industry' while the corpus is polyurethane
internal inconsistency: 'first 10 snapshots ... subsequent 10 ... ratio 2:1' (10:10 is 1:1)
MALE is described as a 'mean squared difference between logarithms', conflating absolute and squared error; the log offset is unstated (counts can be 0)
the 2023-2027 'future trajectory' demonstration cannot be scored against ground truth for out-years
citation counts treated as a proxy for value/impact; the cited literature supports correlation, not equivalence
domain is Chinese-dominated polyurethane patents, not medical devices
leakage_risks: features must come only from snapshots <= T; any pooling of the evaluation window into node features leaks the label
left/right censoring: patents published 2020-2023 have short citation windows, biasing new-vs-grown comparisons
in MedRadar reuse, the evaluation window must be strictly after both the feature window and the record's availability/ingestion time
methods.reproduction_status: NOT_REPRODUCED and explicitly not claimed. No code, no data, unreadable equations, commercial source corpus. The evaluation protocol and metric/curve logic were independently implemented and self-tested on synthetic data: Richards fit recovers a known K=250 with R^2=1.000; MALE hand-check |ln5-ln4|=0.223144; subtask gap (2-4 citations belong to neither new nor grown) preserved; synthetic backtest shows RMSLE rising monotonically with horizon (0.521, 0.750, 1.236, 1.401) as the paper qualitatively reports.
methods.decision_reason: Fails the reproducibility bar outright (no code, no data, equation images, commercial database) and its target construct, patent citations, has no counterpart in MedRadar's regulatory-event data; the model also needs GPU compute that is out of scope. Only the multi-horizon evaluation protocol and the curve/metric machinery transfer, and those are implemented and self-tested here.

methods.name: Clinical specialty expansion of FDA-authorized AI/ML-enabled medical devices 1995-2025
methods.licence_or_terms: Open-access journal article (JMIR). Underlying FDA registry records are US-government public-domain data. The article's formal licence block was not separately read; reuse claims should be checked against the journal's terms.
methods.access_barrier: None for article or data (free, no registration). The 17x4 panel table needed to recompute Era-1 HHI is in Multimedia Appendix 1 (Table S2) and was not retrieved.
methods.core_method: 1430 FDA AI/ML device authorisations (final decision <= 2025-12-31, registry downloaded 2026-03-01) stratified into 4 eras by decision date and classified by advisory-committee panel. HHI = sum of squared specialty share fractions over authorisations within an era, with 2000-resample bootstrap 95% CIs and a bootstrap test of the Era3->Era4 change (2 x proportion of resampled differences <= 0, for a decline). Plus Cochran-Armitage trend tests over equal-spaced era scores with Bonferroni across 17 panels, a 2-proportion z test, Wilson CIs, Pearson chi-square with Cramer's V verified by 10,000-replicate Monte Carlo permutation, and a multivariable logistic regression of nonradiology authorisation on era and manufacturer type with cluster-robust SEs, continuous-year and Firth sensitivity analyses.
data_deps: FDA AI-Enabled Medical Devices List (free download, snapshot dated 2026-03-01)
advisory committee panel per device (fallback: product code classification)
submission number, device name, company, pathway (510(k)/De Novo/PMA)
manufacturer attributes for the 4-level firm typology (employees, founding year, IPO stage)
methods.overlap_with_medradar: High. MedRadar already stores the same regulatory substrate: 375,378 events (openfda_device_510k 176,466; openfda_device_pma 57,372; date range 1966-2026), 7,097 product_codes rows with an FDA-style `specialty` column, 5,624 product codes on events, 60 tracks, 89 company keys. Missing versus M6: De Novo events, an AI/ML cohort flag, and full manufacturer coverage.
methods_to_migrate: HHI = sum of squared specialty share fractions per era, with bootstrap CIs and a change test
Cochran-Armitage trend with equal-spaced era scores + Bonferroni across panels
Wilson intervals instead of Wald at small n
Monte Carlo permutation check when expected cell counts are small
share-base sensitivity reporting (pooled 'Other' bucket vs full panel list)
firm-level HHI as an extension M6 did not do (MedRadar has company_key)
limitations: unit is the authorisation, not the product: multiple submissions per product family inflate counts and induce within-firm correlation
specialty is an FDA regulatory panel, not clinical deployment context
registry is a moving download, so 'complete calendar year' claims are relative to the download date
Era-1 HHI (0.181) is not reproducible from the published table; the pooled 'Other (n=9)' row cannot produce it
technology-company OR rests on 13 devices from 5 firms (authors call it 'highly imprecise')
manufacturer classification for low-volume firms relies on founding year and naming conventions
emerging specialties are descriptive Era3->Era4 growth; none survive Bonferroni correction
US-only; authorisation is not adoption
leakage_risks: era must be assigned from decision date, never from ingestion/first_seen timestamps
bootstrap must resample the analysed unit (authorisation), not specialty cells, or CIs are too narrow
multiple authorisations per manufacturer create within-firm correlation that naive SEs ignore
era boundaries chosen after seeing volumes can bake in the result unless pre-registered
methods.reproduction_status: METHOD_REPRODUCED_ON_SYNTHETIC_DATA + FORMULAS_CROSS_CHECKED against the paper's printed statistics. No re-run of the 1430-device study (registry is a moving download and no analysis file was published). Self-test: 56/56 checks. Formula cross-checks: HHI Eras 2-4 reproduce (0.4325 vs 0.427; 0.7381 vs 0.738; 0.6122 vs 0.612); Wilson CI reproduces 74.49%-80.30% vs published 74.5%-80.3%; 2-prop z gives p=0.0011 vs P=.001; Cochran-Armitage Z=+5.300 vs published +5.30. Era 1 does NOT reproduce (0.2234 vs 0.181) and this is reported as a base-of-shares finding, not hidden.
methods.decision_reason: Only one of the four where the method is uniquely and unambiguously specified, needs no paid/GPU resource, and runs on data MedRadar already holds at scale. Four of the five printed statistics reproduce exactly from the paper's own published counts, which validates my implementation of the formulas; the fifth divergence is itself an actionable methodological finding about HHI share bases. Adopt with documented adaptations: unit and censoring discipline, category-granularity disclosure, and a firm-level HHI extension.
